data.name: Temsirolimus
data.description: Intravenous rapamycin ester (CCI-779); mTOR inhibitor approved for advanced renal cell carcinoma.
data.description_beginner: An injectable, water-soluble version of rapamycin. It's an approved mTOR-blocking treatment for advanced kidney cancer.

reading_levels.student: Intravenous rapalog, first mTOR inhibitor approved for advanced renal cell carcinoma.
reading_levels.research: CCI-779; a prodrug converted to sirolimus. Its RCC approval rests on the ARCC trial.

studies.title: Temsirolimus, interferon alfa, or both for advanced renal-cell carcinoma
studies.authors: Hudes G; Carducci M; Tomczak P; Dutcher J; Figlin R; Kapoor A; Staroslawska E; Sosman J; McDermott D; Bodrogi I; Kovacevic Z; Lesovoy V; Schmidt-Wolf IG; Barbarash O; Gokmen E; O'Toole T; Lustgarten S; Moore L; Motzer RJ

evidence.label: Human study
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.finding: Temsirolimus alone extended median overall survival to 10.9 months versus 7.3 months with interferon alfa in poor-prognosis metastatic kidney cancer; rash, hyperglycemia, and hyperlipidemia were more common with temsirolimus.

studies.title: SPOP-mediated ZMYND8 ubiquitination and phase separation exclusion drives mTOR inhibitor resistance in kidney cancer
studies.authors: Tang B; Sun R; Shao J; Wu QY; Yan Y; Wang D; Yu Z; Hu L; Chen Y; Liao C; Wei Q; Bao Y; Huang H

evidence.label: Animal model
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.model_system: ccRCC cell lines (in vitro); mouse xenograft tumors treated with a NEK7-targeting PROTAC
studies.finding: Identifies a mechanism of mTOR-inhibitor (everolimus/temsirolimus) resistance in clear cell renal cell carcinoma: SPOP-driven K63-linked ubiquitination of ZMYND8 excludes it from phase-separation compartments, enabling a ZMYND8-ZHX2 complex that drives NEK7 transcription and alternative p70S6K activation independent of mTOR inhibition. A NEK7-targeting PROTAC restored everolimus sensitivity in ccRCC cells and mouse tumors, nominating NEK7 as a target to overcome mTOR-inhibitor resistance.

studies.title: Enhanced sensitivity of PTEN-deficient tumors to inhibition of FRAP/mTOR
studies.authors: Neshat MS; Mellinghoff IK; Tran C; Stiles B; Thomas G; Petersen R; Frost P; Gibbons JJ; Wu H; Sawyers CL

evidence.label: Animal model
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.model_system: Isogenic PTEN+/+ and PTEN-/- mouse cells and human cancer cell lines, in vitro and as tumours in mice; CCI-779
studies.finding: Tested whether tumour cells that have lost PTEN depend more on mTOR. The rapamycin analogue CCI-779 (temsirolimus) blocked growth of PTEN-null cells and tumours preferentially, and reversed the extra tumour growth caused by constitutively active Akt, placing mTOR downstream of Akt in tumour formation. PTEN loss went with higher S6 kinase activity and S6 phosphorylation. Sensitivity was not explained by how well the drug blocked S6 phosphorylation, since S6 was inhibited in sensitive and resistant lines alike. Boundary: worked from the abstract only (scanned PMC record); mouse and human cell lines and mouse tumour models, not patients.

studies.title: Randomized phase II study of multiple dose levels of CCI-779, a novel mammalian target of rapamycin kinase inhibitor, in patients with advanced refractory renal cell carcinoma
studies.authors: Atkins MB; Hidalgo M; Stadler WM; Logan TF; Dutcher JP; Hudes GR; Park Y; Liou SH; Marshall B; Boni JP; Dukart G; Sherman ML

evidence.label: Human study
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.model_system: Humans: 111 patients with advanced refractory renal cell carcinoma, randomised to three weekly IV doses of temsirolimus (CCI-779)
studies.finding: In this randomised phase II trial, 111 patients with advanced renal cell carcinoma that had progressed on earlier therapy received temsirolimus (CCI-779) at 25, 75 or 250 mg as a weekly intravenous infusion. There was no control arm: randomisation compared dose levels only. The objective response rate was 7% (1 complete and 7 partial responses), with minor responses in a further 26%; median time to progression was 5.8 months and median survival 15.0 months. Neither efficacy nor toxicity differed significantly between the three doses, which supported taking the lowest dose (25 mg) forward. The commonest side effects were rash (76%), mouth sores (70%), weakness (50%) and nausea (43%); the commonest grade 3-4 events were high blood glucose (17%), low phosphate (13%), anaemia (9%) and high triglycerides (6%). Boundary: patients with advanced, previously treated kidney cancer; no placebo or active comparator, so survival figures cannot be attributed to the drug; risk-group analysis was retrospective.

relations.mechanism: Temsirolimus is the intravenous rapamycin analogue, and, to our knowledge, the first mTOR inhibitor to show an overall-survival benefit in a randomised trial.
relations.mechanism_beginner: Temsirolimus is the IV version of rapamycin and, as far as we know, the first mTOR-blocking drug shown to help patients live longer in a controlled trial (in advanced kidney cancer).
relations.boundary: HUD2007 shows the clinical effect (overall survival in poor-prognosis metastatic kidney cancer). It did not measure mTORC1 activity; that temsirolimus inhibits mTORC1 rests on the FKBP12-dependent mechanism it shares with rapamycin.
relations.note: 2026-10-10: beginner text hedged to match the expert text ('to our knowledge'); boundary added that the cited trial is clinical, not pharmacodynamic.

relations.mechanism: In poor-prognosis renal cancer, temsirolimus improved overall survival against interferon - the hardest endpoint there is.
relations.mechanism_beginner: In hard-to-treat kidney cancer, temsirolimus helped patients live longer compared with an older drug.
relations.boundary: Poor-prognosis patients specifically; the combination arm did not beat temsirolimus alone.
relations.note: Overall survival, not a surrogate. Worth pointing at.
